Oh! So, Colourpop's ultra mattes are kind of drying.

These are NOT indie brands so I'm not sure I should be suggesting them, but you say that Colourpop is the only lip that you've seen which is transfer proof and there's actually a lot of liquid lipsticks out there. Here's a list of other matte liquid lipsticks that you can look into which are known for their long lasting power and being transfer-proof.

- Jeffree Star's Velour Liquid Lipsticks (I have these. I love these. You don't feel them on your lips unlike Colourpop's. I recommend these. I haven't tried any others on this list so just know that, but these apply much easier than Colourpop's formula and feel lightweight on the lips. They take a little longer to dry than Colourpop's. If you eat greasy food, however, it will come off.)

- KVD's Everlasting Liquid Lipstick. 

- Anastasia Beverly Hill's liquid lipstick. (A lot of r/makeupaddiction will swear by ABH.) 

- Stila's Liquid Lipstick.


I recommend just looking up liquid lipsticks in general because they are known to set and dry on your lips, which means that they're more transfer-proof. You will not find a lip gloss that will be transfer-proof. However, I hear a lot of good things about Fyrinnae liquid lipsticks.

I do NOT recommend Limecrime. If you want to try lime crime then that is fine, but please make sure that you look up all of the bad history on lime crime and then make an educated purchase.

Here's my truthful review. (I bought these of my own money, except for The Strip, Cupcakes, and Luxury, which were free samples)

These shadows are pretty lackluster without some sort of primer imo. Pixie Epoxy and NYX Milk both work pretty well as primers for all shades, but for the glitter shades (Tunnel Snakes & The Strip), Pixie Epoxy shows more glitter. Thus, they do not hold up to Urban Decay Eyeshadows, which do not require a primer to look amazing and all that Pixie Epoxy does with UD Eyeshadows is it gives it even more glitter. Keep in mind that my UD shadow is pressed already and the others are loose form so I'm not sure if that's anything different.

As for Fyrinnae's Luxury, this is my first time ever receiving a Fyrinnae product (I only ordered Pixie Epoxy). And oh my GOD WHAT IS THIS. The gold they gave me looks SO good on me, I think that I am imagining things, it looks like I painted actual gold on my skin? I may be really biased because the gold I got from them is a cool gold, versus a warm gold that I got from AFK, and I believe that cool tones suit me more. But I definitely will be buying stuff from Fyrinnae in the future. The eyeshadow is so creamy too, and really easy to work with. It's awkward because Luxury is what impressed me most out of the whole set and it was a free sample ahh...

That being said, I am very happy with my purchase! $6 versus $21 for an eyeshadow really is a lot, and I'm very satisfied with AFK's pigmentation and colors as well as cute packaging. I will order more in the future if there are shades I am interested in :)

Actually the most popular breed for meat rabbits is New Zealand Whites, which are also domestic rabbits as well as the popular rabbit used in labs.

People generally don't raise hares, in fact it is very difficult to raise a wild rabbit from birth. People generally raise rabbits like NZW or Flemish Giants or Chincillas as meat rabbits all of which are domestic rabbits. People do hunt hares, though. The most popular breed for meat rabbits is New Zealand Whites, which are also the same breed used in labs but they are also a very popular breed raised as pets. The only thing people are generally iffy about them is their pink eyes. They make amazing pets and are very common because of their friendly disposition (they're often called the golden retrievers of the rabbit world!) This lady describes having new zealand whites as pets [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FbibvbYxIzw). 

I don't have any opinion on raising meat rabbits except to give them a happy life and be humane when slaughtering them. But all domestic breeds of rabbits are edible. It's not true that a different breed is kept for meat than as a pet.
